Entry.Text: The closer you are to a race on the wheel above, the faster you can build their units and the cheaper it is to fortify their cities.
The following is a brief summary of a combat major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines lots of high level units with extra combat swings.
Weakness: Only hero based magic spells and very low mana regeneration.
Favors: Players who like to create a few power stacks of high level units without using magic.

Playtips: Upgrade Weaponmaster before Morale. Take all capitol unit upgrades and make power stacks of capitol units. Use full stacks where ever possible to take advantage of Weaponmaster. Consider razing nearby cities to attach more sites to your capitol. Combat, Nature and Necromancy make great minors.
The following is a brief summary of a divine major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines lots of persistant spells with extra combat life and unit movement.
Weakness: Lack of battle spells and weak capitol city units makes defending tough.
Favors: Players who like increased movement and attacking over defending.

Playtips: Upgrade Crusader before Divine. Always attack instead of defending to get the Crusader life bonus. Use Endurance to expand rapidly. Research persistant spells first. Paladin, Inspiration, White Ward, Endurance and the Altar are key spells. Combat and Divine make great minors.
The following is a brief summary of a rune major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines good mixture of spells with lots of extra money and magic item offers. Shines in teamplay games.
Weakness: Does not do anything exceptionally well.
Favors: Players who like a lot of magic items and money for upgrading cities.

Playtips: Upgrade Merchant and Rune equally. Buy or build lots of heroes and make sure they have empty spots for a merchant's items. Use Slow to reduce enemy expansion early on. Earth Spirit, Hail, Earthpower, Slow and the Altar are key spells. Combat, Divine and Rune make great minors.
The following is a brief summary of a nature major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines lots of great battle spells with extra defensive life and tower damage.
Weakness: Worst Altar spell and high mana cost for battle spells can make attacking hard.
Favors: Players who like to capture one city at a time and fortify it heavily.

Playtips: Upgrade Defender before Nature. Always place stacks in cities to get the Defender life bonus. Cast Growth early/often to speed expansion. Upgrade cities or increase tower life. Growth, Blessing of Iris, Herbalism and Accurary are key spells and avoid the Altar. Nature and Summoning make great minors.
The following is a brief summary of a summoning major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines lots of summoning spells with extra combat and life to those summoned units.
Weakness: Often must chose between summoning units or using other spells due to high mana costs.
Favors: Rush style players who like to summon high level units early and often.

Playtips: Upgrade Gate before Summoning. Send a flying unit behind enemy lines and cast Summon Minion/PyroHydra. Use Ring of Fire on units in cities. Use Enrage to kill archery units. Ring of Fire, Summon Minion, Enrage, PyroHydra, Doombat and the Altar are key spells. Combat and Summoning make great minors.
The following is a brief summary of a necromancy major Warlord's skills.
Strengths: Combines good mixture of summoning and battle spells with magic resistance for units.
Weakness: A lot of Undead or Evil only spells.
Favors: Players who like spell variety and magic resistance.

Playtips: Upgrade Anti-Magic and Necromancy equally. Deathplague when playing Undead is devastating. Use Flaming Skull early for siege help. Send a flying unit and cast Raise Champion to buy distant cities. Deathplague, Flaming Skulls, Phantom Steed, Mana Drain and the Altar are key spells. Combat and Necromancy make great minors.
A Warlord's minor skills can be broken down into 4 basic playing styles.
Fame/Chaos: For players who like a lot of allies and lowering their enemies morale.
Glory: For players who like a lot of heroes.
Engineer: For players who like upgrading cities, towers and sites.
Archmage: For players who like to cast a lot of magic spells.

Every time a unit hits an enemy in combat, it compares Morale scores with that enemy. If its Morale is higher, then it has a chance at a second free attack. The bigger the difference, the greater the chance of a second attack.
There are a number of factors that contribute to your final Morale score :
Your Warlord's Morale skill and enemy Chaos skills
Various buildings in capital cities
Items possessed by your heroes and enemy heroes
+1 for each Statue attached to your cities
+2 if a group has all creatures from the same race
+1 if a group has all creatures from adjacent races
-1 if a group has creatures from opposite races
-3 if your Warlord has been slain
Any Warlord who has chosen one of the 5 magic skills for his primary or secondary ability, may cast spells.
Spells must be learnt before they are cast. More powerful spells take longer to learn. If your Warlord is killed no new spells may be learned or cast.
When you cast a spell, you do so from your currently-selected group or city. If neither are selected, then it will be cast from your capital.
The further away from your capital that you cast a spell, the more mana it will cost.
Your heroes may also cast a limited number of hero specific spells that can be learned by any Warlord.
Each spell you learn has a mana cost. More powerful spells cost more mana to cast.
Your Warlord regenerates mana every turn. He can increase his mana regeneration in a number of ways :
Each Mana Crystal adds +1
Buildings in the capital
Items possessed by your heroes
The Archmage skill
Each Library you own adds +1
The mana cost of a spell is what it will cost you to cast it in your capital city. If you cast it elsewhere, the following modifiers will apply :
Summoning in a nearby city : +4
Summoning in a nearby group : +6
Summoning in a distant city : +8
Summoning in a distant group : +12
Invocation in a nearby city : +5
Invocation in a nearby group : +8
Invocation in a distant city : +10
Invocation in a distant group : +15

Each time a new unit enters battle, the tower will shoot at the attacker. The damage done, depends upon the level of the city:
Level 1 City: 1-3 points
Level 2 City: 1-4 points
Level 3 City: 1-5 points
Level 4 City: 1-6 points
Capital City: 1-10 points

The Combat score for a unit determines how well it performs in combat. The greater the difference in combat scores, the more likely one unit is to hit another.
When a unit hits an enemy, it does 5-8 points of damage to that creature's Life score. If the unit misses, it only does 1 point of damage.
Every time a unit hits a foe, there is 10% chance of a critical hit, doing 12 points of damage (instead of 5-8).
The higher its Life score, the longer a unit can survive in combat. All damage that a unit takes is subtracted from its Life total.
Damage on a unit does not heal naturally until the beginning of the owner's following turn.
This is a skill available only to Orcs. It does not confer any special abilities apart from increasing both Combat and Life at the same time.

During the course a battle, your Warlord will learn many spells. Each of these spells must first be researched.
At the start of each battle, and every time you learn a new spell, you will be given a choice of up to 8 more spells to learn.

The rarer and more powerful a spell, the longer it takes to learn. However, if your Warlord has gained skill in a particular sphere of magic, the time to learn spells from this sphere will grow shorter.
You should now choose one of the spells on offer, and then continue with the game.
You begin a battle in control of your Capital City. You can always tell a capital because of the tiny shooting stars coming from it.
You must look after this city. If an enemy captures it, you will lose the battle!
Your Warlord and any starting troops will be inside this city. Your Warlord cannot leave the capital, but all your other troops can.
Start by selecting your capital (left click on it).
You are now inside your city.
On the right you can see Production. On the Left you can see your Troops. We will start with production.
Each city, depending on its level, can build from 2-6 different types of units. Each unit takes a certain number of turns to produce.
Select a unit to produce by left clicking on it (right clicking on it will give you more detailed information).
On the left you can see the troops in this city. They are either below the Tent or the Tower.
Units in the Tent are able to move out. Units in the Tower are garrisoned and must be placed in the Tent before moving out. Your Warlord is a special unit and may never leave the Tower.
Move some units out of the City by right clicking twice on the map (once to set the path, once to move there).
Remember this : Left click to select things; Right click to move them (unless you change this in the Options Menu).
Warlords is mostly about fighting: attacking enemy cities and attacking guardians in ruins.
To expand your empire, you will need to first attack neutral cities (the ones with gray flags).
You will also want to search ruins - killing their guardians so you can get to their treasures.
Initiating combat is exactly like moving, right click once on your target, then right click again to move there and fight.
You are now in the combat screen.
Only one side can survive. There is no retreat.
You choose one unit at a time to go and fight. If that unit is slain, you can choose your next one, and so on. This continues until one side is wiped out.
Many of your units will have special abilities (you can right click on their portraits for more details). These abilities will be used automatically as required.
You have conquered this city! It, and any buildings attached to it, are yours.
You will now be presented with a number of options. Some of them may affect the city's level, and some may even raze the city.
In general, the more damage you do to the city, the more gold you can pillage from it.
But remember, the more damage you do, the less troops it can produce and the weaker its defences.
You have defeated the guardians of this ruin.
Every ruin contains treasure. It might be gold, mana crystals, allies, heroes or experience points.
Once ruins are searched, they cannot be searched again. However, every so often some monsters will move back in to an explored ruin, bringing new treasure with them.
If you have a city attached to a shrine, you can obtain a Quest.
Getting a quest entitles you to search special hidden ruins on the map. If you can search all 4 of these ruins, then you will receive a very big reward.
To get a quest, right click (to bring up the right-click menu) and select the Get Quest option.
You can bring up a list of useful commands in the game known as the Popup Menu. Usually this will present you with a list of options, including various reports.

There are a number of different ways to access the popup menu : the button in the top left, holding down CTRL while clicking on the map, or even by right clicking on the map when nothing else is selected.
There are also many things in the game that you can right click on to get more information, such as unit portraits (to get detailed stats) or skills (to see descriptions).
You have learned a new spell. When you want to cast it, use the right-click menu and choose Cast Spell.
You will continue to learn new spells during a battle until you have learnt all the spells that you can cast!
You may cast any spell while in the world map, however while in combat, you may only cast Battle Spells.
There are two very important resources in the game: Gold and Mana.
The bottom control panel shows you your gold and mana totals, along with income and upkeep.
Each city you own generates gold. Each unit you control costs gold. If you have no gold, then you may not produce any more troops.
Mana is different. It is used to cast spells and regenerates naturally over time. To view info about your mana, hold the mouse over the mana total and look in the help bar at the very bottom.
Some spells are Battle Spells. These can be cast in combat.
Other spells are Enchantments. These can be cast any time, and are continuous (but cost mana to keep running).

Some spells have a location (such as Summoning Spells or Damage Spells). These spells will be cast from the currently-selected group or city. If nothing is selected, they will be cast from your capital.
The further from your capital they are cast, the more these spells cost in mana.
Waypoints are a way for you automate sending troops to your frontline.
From within the waypoint menu, left click on a city and then right click on it target. All troops produced there will now move towards the target automatically.
If city A points to city B, and city B points to city C, then all units produced in A will follow the waypoints to city C.
You can also set waypoints from within the city menu, by left and right clicking on the mini map in the bottom right.
When all of your troops have finished moving you will want to end your turn. You do this by clicking the shield button in the bottom right.
To find out if you have any troops who have not yet moved, you can click the Next Group button in the bottom panel (fourth button from the right).
Remember that any units a garrison (in the Tower inside a city) will not show up with the Next Group button.
One of your troops has gained a level.
When your units level up, they may improve a number of things - either their Combat score, their Life points, or their Special Ability.
To find out information about special abilities on this screen, you can simply right-click on them.
Keeping a high Morale is important to your success in combat. Troops with high Morale get extra attacks.
Your current Morale is displayed in the bottom control panel. Many things can affect it, including how many statues you own, as well as what mix of troops you have in a group.
For more detailed information about Morale, see its entry in the Play Tips section of this help menu.
The Mini Map in the top right corner is very useful for watching the progress of your enemies.
You can also use the Mini Map to quickly navigate around the map by left clicking on it.
The size of the mini map can be changed by either right clicking on it, or by pressing the M key.
Victory is simple in Warlords IV.
All you need to do is to capture all of the enemy capital cities before they capture yours.
Beware though, each enemy capital has a powerful Warlord inside, waiting to defend it.
You will have noticed by now that different cities seem to have varying levels of defence.
You can increase your city's defence by Fortifying it. Right click on your city and select the Fortify Option.
Fortification costs money though. Given enough money, you can even build back most cities that were previously razed.
Of course you can also raze cities to deny your opponents the chance to capture them.
A hero with Fear subtracts from the Combat skill of all enemy units in battle. Only the highest Fear skill is used for this (it is not cumulative).
Level 1 : -1 Enemy Combat
Level 2 : -2 Enemy Combat
Level 3 : -3 Enemy Combat
Level 4 : -4 Enemy Combat
Level 5 : -5 Enemy Combat
A hero with Leadership adds to the Combat Skill and movement of his group. Only the highest Leadership skill is used for this (it is not cumulative).
Level 1 : +1 Combat and +1 Speed for the group
Level 2 : +2 Combat and +1 Speed for the group
Level 3 : +2 Combat and +2 Speed for the group
Level 4 : +3 Combat and +2 Speed for the group
Level 5 : +3 Combat and +3 Speed for the group
A hero may summon flying mount via a spell. This mount carries *only* the hero who summoned it. If multiple heroes want to fly they must all summon their own mounts.
If the mount is killed or the mount and hero are seperated over water/lava the hero will die from the fall to the ground.
The type of mount is based on the heroes alignment and level.
Hero Level 1-4 : Level 1 Mount
Hero Level 5-9 : Level 2 Mount
Hero Level 10+ : Level 3 Mount
Good : Summons a Pegasi mount
Neutral : Summons a Storm Dragon Mount
Evil : Summons a Wyvern Mount

Heroes may cast spells from the heroes magic sphere (orange icons). These spells must be researched like spells from other magic spheres with the difference being all Warlords get access to the hero sphere.
Hero based spells can only be cast when a hero is present in the stack. If the Warlord dies these may still be cast but no further research for new hero spells can be done.
The hero spell list is:
Heroes Mount : Summons a flying mount for the hero (creature spell)
Heroic Strike : Doubles critical hit chance for all units (battle spell)
Heroic Presence : Adds +2 to morale for all units (battle spell)
Heroic Expertise : Adds +1 to damage for all units (battle spell)
Heroes Feast : Adds +2 life for all units (battle spell)

The terrain used for combat is the terrain the defender occupies. This will be displayed on the combat screen.
Often more than one terrain type will be listed. Those combats will have effects from multiple terrain types apply.
Special Combat Effects : These apply in all terrains.
Units with Archery skill : +1 Archery versus Fliers
An item with the City Gold power increases the amount of gold you receive from each of your cities every turn.
An item with the Divine power increases your Divine Magic skill. It does not grant the power to cast Divine spells if your warlord doesn't have a Divine major or minor skill.
An item with the Escape power allows its wearer to escape from battle before they are killed. It will be used automatically by the hero and may only be used once.
It does not prevent death from Assassination, Death Gaze or Archery.
An item with the Fealty power can be used to automatically purchase a neutral city of any race. It may only be used once so chose carefully when to use it.
An item with the Move Bonus power allows its wearers stack to treat all terrain as if it were plains.
An item with the Nature power increases your Nature Magic skill. It does not grant the power to cast Nature spells if your warlord doesn't have a Nature major or minor skill.
An item with the Necromancy power increases your Necromancy Magic skill. It does not grant the power to cast Necromancy spells if your warlord doesn't have a Necromancy major or minor skill.
An item with the Recruit Allies power increases the chance of allies offering to join you each turn but does not reduce their cost.
An item with the Rune power increases your Rune Magic skill. It does not grant the power to cast Rune spells if your warlord doesn't have a Rune major or minor skill.
An item with the Summoning power increases your Summoning Magic skill. It does not grant the power to cast Summoning spells if your warlord doesn't have a Summoning major or minor skill.
An item with the XP Bonus power increases the amount of experience given from each combat.

The chance to hit an opponent in combat is based on the difference between the strengths of the two units. Subtract the weaker units strength from the stronger and consult the following table to find the stronger units chance to hit (as a percentage).
The weaker units chance to hit is 100-(stronger units chance to hit).
Ex 1: Two equal strength units fight. The difference in strength is 0. So both units have a 50% chance to hit.
Ex 2: Two units with strengths 15 and 5 fight. The difference in strength is 10. The stronger unit has an 84% chance to hit and the weaker unit has a 16% chance to hit.
Morale can range from -5 to 15 depending on various bonuses and penalties.
The side with the higher morale has a chance for an extra attack every combat round. That chance is (the difference in Morale X 3)%.
Ex 1: Two sides with morale 10 and 5 fight. The difference in morale is 5. So the side with 10 morale has a 5X3=15% chance for an extra attack every combat round.
The base chances for hero, mercenary and merchant offers are:
Hero: 20% - 1% for each existing hero (including retinue, summoned and built heroes)
Mercenary: 20%
Merchant: 20%
These chances can go up based on Warlord skills, Inns attached to your cities and items possessed by your heroes.
Only one of these offers can happen in a turn. The offer check order each turn is hero, mercenary and then merchant.
